subject: Urgent: Sunrise Labs AZ1 latency + error surge — proposed cross-region cutover & exec bridge
messages:
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: [P0] Sunrise Labs — spike in 5xx + p95 latency in us-west-2 AZ1

Marcus / Team,

Heads-up: Sunrise Labs (renewal Q3) is reporting a sharp latency and error-rate spike focused on us-west-2 AZ1. Ops alert: 15% 5xx across text-generation endpoints starting ~07:50 PT and p95 latency jumped 3.8x. I've attached the error dump and a snapshot of their SLO dashboard.

Customer impact notes from platform@sunrise.lab: many requests failing with 502/524; traffic volume is within normal bounds but we see kernel-level queuing and token-timeouts for long-context requests. Initial triage suggests an AZ-level ingress/backplane degradation rather than a model issue.

Asking for:
- Exec bridge asap (they're requesting C-suite visibility)
- Quick decision on cross-region steering (can we shift to us-west-1 as a short-term mitigation?)
- Possible one-time credit ask preemptively (they mentioned contract sensitivity)

I've already run a quick sample and included the CSV. If we decide to steer, we should:
1) Authorize immediate routing policy override for Sunrise (pin to us-west-1)
2) Enable degraded-mode quantized fallback for high-latency requests to preserve throughput
3) Start a short customer-facing note (what we can do, ETA)

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-14T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [P0] Sunrise Labs — spike in 5xx + p95 latency in us-west-2 AZ1

Thanks Soojin — good catch and thanks for the data. I'm elevating to an exec bridge and want to move quickly. Proposed immediate actions (we can adapt during bridge):

- Authorization: Approve cross-region steer to us-west-1 for Sunrise Labs. This will be a targeted routing rule for their org-id, ttl 4h with manual rollback.
- Traffic shaping: Apply degraded-mode (quantized model variant) for requests > 512 tokens to reduce GPU kernel pressure.
- Observability: Increase log-levels and pin a short retention for detailed traces (7 days) for this org only so we can correlate end-to-end.
- Customer communication: Laura, can you draft a 30–60 minute outbound to Alice with what we are doing and an ETA for full remediation? Keep tone apologetic, factual, and include the option for a credit if the incident meets SLA breach thresholds.

I'll schedule a 11:00 PT exec bridge (invite forthcoming) and will add CTO and Head of Reliability for visibility. Jonas — please attach the short runbook snippet for cross-region cutover and an expected time-to-stabilize estimate.

If we need to enable emergency capacity or burst into Dedicated pools, call it out in the bridge.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Date: 2028-08-14T09:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [P0] Sunrise Labs — spike in 5xx + p95 latency in us-west-2 AZ1

Quick tech summary and recommended cutover steps:

Findings so far:
- Metrics show node-level CPU steal and NVMe queue saturation limited to AZ1 subfleet; other AZs in us-west-2 are normal.
- KV cache hit ratio dipped ~22% which explains the token amplification for long chats.
- No model regressions in the last 48h; model latencies in us-west-1 are stable.

Recommend immediate (10–15 min) actions to reduce customer impact:
1) Short-term routing: Apply organization-scoped route override -> redirect 90% of new sessions to us-west-1. Keep 10% for canary traffic to validate stateful session transfer.
2) Enable quantized fallback (qa-rtq) for sessions with prompt length >512 tokens to reduce per-token GPU time.
3) If failover shows successful canary, increase to 100% and mark the us-west-2 AZ1 nodes for a soft drain with telemetry collection.
4) Post-cutover: run KV cache warmup job for Sunrise sessions (approx 20–30 min) and monitor p50/p95.

Estimated stabilization: 30–45 minutes after cutover if route completes cleanly. I attached the internal runbook for cross-region failover.

Attachments: runbook-cross-region-failover.pdf

Jonas Weber
VP, Reliability Engineering
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Marcus / team,

Thanks for the rapid response and proposed plan — we appreciate the transparency. A few things from our side:
- Current observed impact: p95 latency ~3.5–4x baseline for the past hour, errors ~12–18% depending on endpoint (most user impact on our chat features).
- Business impact: We have a product demo today at 13:00 PT that depends on low-latency responses; this is high-visibility for us.
- Credits: If this is classified as an SLA incident, we'll expect the contract remedies. Please confirm the process and timeline to file a claim.

Please keep us posted on the bridge results and the expected user-visible restoration window. We are available for the 11:00 PT bridge.

—
